title: Hardness of Approximating Quantum Code Distance Beyond $\sqrt{N}$
abstract: We study the computational complexity of approximating the minimum distance of a stabilizer code. Classically, the minimum distance problem is NP-hard to approximate even to within an additive gap linear in the block length. For quantum codes, however, the reductions of Kapshikar and Kundu and of Grigorescu, Jha and Samperton reach only an additive $O(\sqrt{N})$ gap in the block length $N$. We close this gap and, in a separate direction, initiate the fine-grained study of the problem.   We show that no randomized algorithm approximates the distance to within an additive $αN$, for a constant $α> 0$, unless $\mathsf{NP} \subseteq \mathsf{coRP}$. In the fine-grained setting, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, no randomized $2^{(1-\varepsilon)κ}\,\mathrm{poly}(N)$-time algorithm computes the distance of a code with $κ$ logical qubits unless SETH falls; and no randomized $2^{o(N)}$-time algorithm approximates the distance to within a linear additive gap, on instances where block length, number of logical qubits, and gap are simultaneously linear, unless non-uniform Gap-ETH falls.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the computational hardness of approximating the minimum distance of quantum stabilizer codes. It closes a prior theoretical gap by proving that achieving a linear approximation gap requires solving problems at the level of $	ext{NP}$-hardness. The results establish deep connections between quantum error correction and foundational complexity theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational complexity of approximating the minimum distance of a stabilizer quantum code (QMDP).
main_result: It establishes strong hardness results, showing that approximating the distance to within a linear additive gap ($\alpha N$) is $	ext{NP}$-hard unless $	ext{NP} \subseteq 	ext{coRP}$, and provides fine-grained lower bounds based on complexity assumptions like SETH.
method: The authors use complexity-theoretic reductions, mapping hard classical problems (like $k$-SAT) to the quantum distance problem via Code from Graph (CWS) constructions.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum stabilizer codes, which are defined by an abelian subgroup of the Pauli group on $N$ qubits. The distance is the minimum weight of an error not in the stabilizer group.
key_observables: The quantum minimum distance, qdist(Q), is the primary observable of interest.
important_parameters: Block length ($N$), number of logical qubits ($\kappa$), and the approximation gap ($\alpha N$).
main_assumptions: The hardness results rely on strong complexity assumptions, including $	ext{NP} \subseteq 	ext{coRP}$, randomized SETH, and non-uniform Gap-ETH.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon prior work by showing how to close the gap in previous $\sqrt{N}$ bounds, establishing hardness for linear gaps, and then proceeding to fine-grained analyses using various complexity assumptions.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental computational limits on the efficiency of quantum error correction, which is crucial for understanding the feasibility of large-scale quantum computation.
